key_insight: A Gaussian surface bump significantly accelerates vortex-induced transition and three-dimensionality while preserving the spatio-temporal wave front characteristic of a nonmodal response.
engineering_relevance: Predicting transition under combined surface roughness and free-stream vortical disturbances requires accounting for their interaction and rapid development of three-dimensional flow.
method: Solve the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations using 2D and 3D direct numerical simulations.
Model a semi-infinite flat plate with a Gaussian bump and a convecting vortex of fixed strength and sign.
Analyze instantaneous flow features, vorticity dynamics, and nonlinear receptivity.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four stages: roughness-generated vortical disturbances, spatio-temporal amplification, wave-front emergence with unsteady separation bubbles, and bubble merging into turbulent spots.
watch_item: Results concern a specific bump and vortex configuration; the abstract provides no quantitative transition shifts or validation metrics for broader generalization.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Vortex-Induced Instability Over a Semi-Infinite Flat Plate with Discrete Roughness
